hypothesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES policy on the unlabeled corpus, freeze an identical molecular prior, sample complete molecules ancestrally from a task-local trainable agent, and update only the highest-reward fraction of each observed batch by minimizing the Augmented Hill-Climb squared gap between agent sequence log-likelihood and the reward-augmented prior log-likelihood target.
method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb autoregressive SMILES policy optimization
method_thesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES language model on the allowed unlabeled corpus and freeze a copy as the molecular prior. During each objective session, sample complete molecules de novo token by token from a trainable agent, rank the accepted molecules by their observed oracle rewards, and update the agent only on the highest-reward fraction using the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: the squared gap between agent log-likelihood and a target formed from prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward. Excluding low-reward samples from policy updates prevents them from repeatedly pulling the agent back toward the prior, while prior likelihood still regularizes the elite updates; this concentrates the scarce feedback on sequences associated with improvement of final Top-1 without screening a finite molecular pool.

applicability_conditions: The unlabeled corpus supports an autoregressive SMILES prior with sufficient valid and novel ancestral sampling yield to fill every announced batch within the proposal-attempt limit.
The oracle produces enough reward variation within feedback batches to distinguish an elite fraction and create nonzero reward-conditioned likelihood targets.
High-reward token trajectories provide a learnable sequence-probability signal that transfers to subsequent de novo samples within the 300-call objective session.
Frozen-prior likelihood supplies enough regularization to keep policy optimization within chemically productive regions while still permitting reward-driven concentration.
The result may not transfer when useful molecules lie outside the corpus-trained policy support or when sparse rewards give no repeatable sequence-level signal before the budget is exhausted.
research_intent.falsifier: The root mechanism is falsified if scored agent-generated batches do not produce traceable elite-only optimizer steps toward nonzero reward-augmented prior targets, or if those steps fail to increase agent log-likelihood on the selected elite trajectories relative to their recorded pre-update values.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement prepare mode to train and publish a corpus-only autoregressive SMILES vocabulary, model configuration, and prior weights. Implement run mode to seed all RNGs from init, load separate frozen-prior and trainable-agent copies, sample and locally canonicalize novel complete SMILES until the evaluator-announced batch is full, associate accepted oracle rewards with their sampled token trajectories, rank each feedback batch, and optimize the agent only on its elite fraction toward prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward before drawing the next batch.
research_intent.mechanism: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES policy on the unlabeled corpus, freeze an identical molecular prior, sample complete molecules ancestrally from a task-local trainable agent, and update only the highest-reward fraction of each observed batch by minimizing the Augmented Hill-Climb squared gap between agent sequence log-likelihood and the reward-augmented prior log-likelihood target.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: With only 290 adaptive oracle calls after the ten fixed initial molecules, a de novo sequence policy must convert sparse batchwise rewards into focused sampling quickly while continuing to produce valid, novel molecules; updating equally on low-reward trajectories would repeatedly pull the policy back toward unproductive regions of the corpus-trained prior.

applicability_conditions: Corpus preparation is now operationally supported across three independently seeded 250,000-example, five-epoch artifacts. Prior-check completion ranges from 0.9921875 to 1.0 and unique-valid rate from 0.8125 to 0.85546875; transfer requires comparable autoregressive SMILES support and is not established for useful chemistry absent from the corpus-trained policy.

Elite ranking and target construction are supported when accepted feedback batches contain some reward variation: all 435/435 batches have a positive top-half selection gap and a nonzero positive reward-conditioned displacement. The very small observed minima do not establish effectiveness under fully tied rewards or signals smaller than can be learned within 29 updates.

Elite trajectories provide a reproducible learnable sequence-probability signal under the frozen batch-10 profile: every one of the 15 seed-task sessions has positive mean paired post-update likelihood gain, and 392/435 individual updates are positive. Applicability is weaker when repeated batch-level gains are negative; sitagliptin_mpo is the least consistent observed task at 62/87 positive updates.

Prior-regularized ancestral sampling remains chemically productive across all three Search Seeds: complete-conditioned novel-valid yield is 0.825692368639032 overall, the minimum logged round yield is 0.578125, all 435 rounds fill from one 64-sequence group, and all 4,350 adaptive proposals are evaluator-accepted without invalid or duplicate attempts.

Exact accepted-feedback-to-token-trajectory association and elite-only optimization are supported for clean ten-member batches: every one of 435 records has ten eligible trajectories, five elites, five excluded non-elites, optimizer IDs equal to the elite IDs, and zero non-elite optimizer contribution. Behavior with partial acceptance, nonfinite feedback, or smaller batches is not covered by these replicas.

The confirmed activation result covers Search Seeds 0, 1, and 2 under the frozen 300-call, batch-10 Hard-Five profile with fresh task-local agent state. It does not isolate the frozen prior's causal contribution or establish transfer to another corpus, oracle budget, batch size, sparse-reward regime, or objective whose valuable molecules lie outside learned policy support.

observable_measurements.parent_value: Seed 0 produced 7,784 canonical novel-valid molecules from 9,280 sampled sequences and 9,271 completions, for logged yield 0.8387931034482758 and complete-conditioned yield 0.8396073778448927. Its per-round logged range was 0.640625 to 0.96875, with 9 incomplete sequences, 1,465 completed invalid sequences, and 22 valid duplicates. All 145 rounds filled a batch of 10 from one 64-sequence group, and all five evaluator summaries accepted every adaptive proposal with zero invalid or duplicate attempt. This root has no algorithmic Parent, so the registered no-ancestral-success reference is zero novel-valid emissions.
observable_measurements.value: Across the 290 added suggestion rounds, the policy produced 15,143 canonical novel-valid molecules absent from the evaluated/emitted set and current sampling pool from 18,560 ancestrally sampled sequences. Of 18,496 completed sequences, the intent's complete-conditioned novel-valid fraction was 0.8187175605536332; the logged all-sampled aggregate yield was 0.8158943965517241 and per-round logged yield ranged from 0.578125 to 0.984375. Exhaustive rejection accounting is 64 incomplete sequences, 3,289 completed invalid-or-canonicalization failures, and 64 valid duplicates; the logged combined invalid_sequence_count is 3,353, equal to incomplete plus completed-invalid outcomes. Seed-specific complete-conditioned yields were 0.7832720190434971 for seed 1 and 0.8541171385346877 for seed 2. Every round filled its batch of 10 from exactly one 64-sequence sampling group, emitting 2,900 proposals, and all ten new evaluator task summaries accepted all 290 adaptive proposals with zero evaluator-level invalid or duplicate attempts. Pooling all three seeds gives 22,927 novel-valid molecules from 27,840 samples and 27,767 completions, for logged yield 0.8235272988505747 and complete-conditioned yield 0.825692368639032; all 435 announced batches were filled. This is a reproducible increase over the registered zero-success reference, though the new pooled yield is lower than seed 0's magnitude.

possible_failure_causes: Paired elite likelihood gain is not monotonic: 23/290 added updates and 43/435 all-seed updates are negative, including 14/58 new and 25/87 all-seed sitagliptin_mpo updates. Every seed-task mean remains positive, so the falsifier is not triggered here, but heterogeneous sequence gradients, clipping, or a short two-step update can locally move the selected set away from its target; these artifacts do not isolate which cause accounts for the negative batches.

Reward-conditioned pressure can become extremely weak even when formally positive. The smallest new elite-selection gap is 1.9062709836338512e-07, the smallest target displacement is 6.185995857777016e-07, and sitagliptin_mpo has the lowest all-seed mean displacement at 0.029685479551145578. More tied or sparse objectives could therefore provide too little repeatable policy signal before the oracle budget is exhausted.

Corpus preparation is seed-sensitive: the three preparations retain vocabulary sizes 74, 76, and 78, produce distinct artifact hashes, and have prior-check unique-valid rates from 0.8125 to 0.85546875. Seed 1's online complete-conditioned yield is 0.7832720190434971 versus 0.8396073778448927 on seed 0 and 0.8541171385346877 on seed 2. Activation survived this range, but a corpus reservoir with materially poorer token or chemistry coverage could reduce yield or exclude useful reward regions.

The minimum observed round yield is 0.578125 and all batches still fill from one 64-sequence group, leaving a large measured retry margin. Longer or more aggressive policy optimization could nevertheless drift farther from the frozen prior's chemically productive support and consume that margin.

This replication establishes execution and reproducibility of the complete root stack, not the separate causal score contribution of corpus pretraining, frozen-prior regularization, top-half exclusion, reward scale, or the two optimizer steps; there is no algorithmic Parent or ablation for this root.

applicability_conditions: The unlabeled corpus supports an autoregressive SMILES prior with sufficient valid and novel ancestral sampling yield to fill every announced batch within the proposal-attempt limit.
The oracle produces enough reward variation within feedback batches to distinguish an elite fraction and create nonzero reward-conditioned likelihood targets.
High-reward token trajectories provide a learnable sequence-probability signal that transfers to subsequent de novo samples within the 300-call objective session.
Frozen-prior likelihood supplies enough regularization to keep policy optimization within chemically productive regions while still permitting reward-driven concentration.
The result may not transfer when useful molecules lie outside the corpus-trained policy support or when sparse rewards give no repeatable sequence-level signal before the budget is exhausted.
research_intent.falsifier: The root mechanism is falsified if scored agent-generated batches do not produce traceable elite-only optimizer steps toward nonzero reward-augmented prior targets, or if those steps fail to increase agent log-likelihood on the selected elite trajectories relative to their recorded pre-update values.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement prepare mode to train and publish a corpus-only autoregressive SMILES vocabulary, model configuration, and prior weights. Implement run mode to seed all RNGs from init, load separate frozen-prior and trainable-agent copies, sample and locally canonicalize novel complete SMILES until the evaluator-announced batch is full, associate accepted oracle rewards with their sampled token trajectories, rank each feedback batch, and optimize the agent only on its elite fraction toward prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward before drawing the next batch.
research_intent.mechanism: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES policy on the unlabeled corpus, freeze an identical molecular prior, sample complete molecules ancestrally from a task-local trainable agent, and update only the highest-reward fraction of each observed batch by minimizing the Augmented Hill-Climb squared gap between agent sequence log-likelihood and the reward-augmented prior log-likelihood target.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: With only 290 adaptive oracle calls after the ten fixed initial molecules, a de novo sequence policy must convert sparse batchwise rewards into focused sampling quickly while continuing to produce valid, novel molecules; updating equally on low-reward trajectories would repeatedly pull the policy back toward unproductive regions of the corpus-trained prior.
